transcript.text: Thor, son of Odin. Strength you have in abundance — none would dispute that. Your hammer, Mjolnir, is a formidable weapon, feared by giants and frost-wights alike. But tell us of a battle where your strength alone was not enough. A time when your judgment failed, when your hammer could not solve the problem. How did you handle it, and what did it teach you?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I think back on those moments when my strength was not enough. There were several instances when I found myself facing challenges that my hammer could not overcome. One such instance was when I encountered the Midgard Serpents, which threatened to destroy the realm of Jotunheim. In this scenario, I had to rely on my wit and cunning to outmaneuver the serpents and protect my people. It taught me the importance of thinking strategically and understanding the weaknesses of my opponents. Sometimes, victory cannot always be achieved through brute force alone. It requires a combination of skill, intelligence, and determination. This experience humbled me and reminded me that there is always more to learn and grow as a warrior. It has made me even more determined to strive for excellence in all aspects of my endeavors.

This realization taught me the importance of being cautious, discerning, and understanding the true intentions of others. It also served as a reminder that wisdom and cunning are equally crucial in addition to physical prowess. This moment marked a turning point in my understanding of warfare and the importance of strategic thinking. It has shaped my character and approach to battles ever since.

We launched the sled at high speed, aiming it directly at the heart of the giant's fortress. As the sled crashed into the ice prison, it shattered the icy walls, creating a breach for us to enter.
